description: A `struct` type name colliding with a user procedure raises `ol-duplicate-definition` at phase-1 registration: `foo` is already declared on line 1, so `struct foo` cannot also register a constructor of that name. Ruling #833 rule 6 gives a name the LEARNER already declared its own code, distinct from `ol-reserved-word`'s "OpenLogo owns this name". What this fixture pins is the observable behaviour: the two declarations differ in KIND (`define` then `struct`), which is the cross-kind half of `spec/error-model.md:126` ("a procedure and a struct with the same name in either order"), and `params.original_span` points at the `define`. It does NOT prove the runtime keeps a single first-declaration map internally — two maps with an explicit cross-kind lookup would produce the identical diagnostic, and no source-level fixture can tell them apart. `struct-then-define-duplicate` pins the opposite order, and `data/check/duplicate-definition-across-declaration-slots` pins the same program at check stage.
